title: Clay - open-source ASIP framework for microarchitecture-aware instruction customization with stateful behavior support
problem: Application-specific instruction processors (ASIPs) require manual microarchitecture design and instruction customization. Existing frameworks lack support for stateful behaviors and hardware-software co-optimization.
motivation: A systematic framework can enable rapid ASIP development by automating instruction generation, enabling microarchitecture tuning, and supporting stateful instruction behaviors for specialized workloads.
method: Clay is an open-source toolkit that automates designing ASIPs (application-specific processors—custom chips optimized for a single job). Engineers use it to specify which instructions they want, how those instructions behave in hardware, and how to maintain state (data stored in the processor) across instructions. The toolkit simulates the design and tests different instruction combinations to find the optimal set for the application.
key_novelty: It's an open-source ASIP design toolkit with explicit support for stateful instructions and microarchitecture-aware customization—capabilities existing frameworks lack.
contributions: Open-source ASIP design framework with comprehensive tool chain
Support for stateful instruction specification and hardware state tracking
limitations: Without specific performance metrics, the actual advantages over existing ASIP design flows and scalability to complex instruction sets remain unclear.
